🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 4)
Channel: alert-runtime-monitoring  •  bug-type guess: unknown  •  alerts in group: 3

Symptoms:
  - 3 Datadog-bot alerts in #alert-runtime-monitoring within 5m08s (12:29:59Z / 12:33:24Z / 12:35:07Z), all `bot_id=B063S8NBW0M`
  - Slack MCP returned all 3 with redacted bodies (recurring gap) — no monitor name, no metric, no service tag extractable from the messages themselves
  - No DD error logs in `env:prod` during 12:25–12:40Z window (zero hits)
  - No DD monitors currently in `Alert` state covering the window (only 2 stale: id 227951254 last 2025-10-16; id 240123515 last 2025-12-15)

Trace IDs: none — no error logs to sample from
Likely cause: inconclusive. Closest temporal correlation is `[Synthetics] Method UI Grid and Dropdown Performance Test Midnight run` (monitor 123495390) which last triggered at exactly **12:30:00Z** (No Data) — but that monitor is `team:qa` and normally routes to #alert-system, not #alert-runtime-monitoring, so the correlation is suggestive, not proven. Pattern of 3 alerts in 5min with no operator engagement and no downstream error signature is consistent with a single monitor flapping (Alert → No Data → recovery).
Suggested next action: open the #alert-runtime-monitoring messages directly in Slack (links below) to recover the monitor identity — the bot can't read the block content. If it is the synthetics flap, mute or widen threshold.

  • DD Synthetics 123495390 (candidate): https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/123495390
  • DD logs (env:prod errors, alert window): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=env%3Aprod%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1779539100000&to_ts=1779540900000&live=false

Score breakdown: +2 group_size (3 alerts in 5m08s), +2 novel (no KB match, no prior 7d hash)

🚨 *new alert — needs human*  (score: 9)
Channel: alert-system  •  bug-type guess: code  •  alerts in group: 2

Symptoms:
  - 2 Datadog-bot alerts in #alert-system within 3m57s (17:54:29Z + 17:58:26Z), both `bot_id=B011R3D650X`, both block-only (recurring Slack MCP gap)
  - Correlated to DD monitor **115456700 "RTC Screen Load has a high p95 latency"** — `last_triggered_ts=17:58:20Z` (Δ=6s to satellite alert); currently OK
  - Underlying metric: `p95:trace.aspnet_core.request{env:prod,service:runtime-core-api,resource_name:post_/api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*}` spiked to **10.72s at 17:51:00Z** (vs 3s threshold, ratio 2.57×), tail 7.98s @17:51:20Z, recovered to <2s by 17:52:20Z
  - No `service:runtime-core-api status:error` log hits in 17:50–18:05Z window — latency without errors
  - No correlated deploys (runtime-core, m-one, gateway, tables-fields all quiet for 4h+)

Trace IDs: none — no error logs to sample from; DD APM trace search not exposed by `dd_search.py`
Likely cause: ~100-second transient p95 saturation on runtime-core screen-load endpoint (17:50:40–17:52:20Z). 3.5× SLO peak warrants a human look at SQL/IIS/GC metrics around 17:51Z, but absence of errors + short duration + monitor recovered = consistent with momentary saturation (DB query, GC pause, or single slow-tenant burst), not sustained degradation. Comparable in shape to 2026-05-07 incident which was ms-sync-util pool crash, but that one had a co-firing XHR-errors monitor and lasted hours; today's lacks both.
Suggested next action: open DD APM for `runtime-core-api` 17:50–17:53Z → filter traces ≥ 5s on `post_/api/v1/runtime/load/_screenid*` → identify the slow span (SQL vs upstream HTTP vs in-process). If repeats in 24h with same signature, promote to KB.

Source alerts (2 total):
  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/CPHHABKAA/p1779558869342999  (alert-system, 17:54 UTC)
  • https://methodme.slack.com/archives/CPHHABKAA/p1779559106959769  (alert-system, 17:58 UTC)

Evidence:
  • DD monitor 115456700: https://app.datadoghq.com/monitors/115456700 — "RTC Screen Load has a high p95 latency" (OK, last_triggered 17:58:20Z)
  • DD logs (runtime-core errors, alert window): https://app.datadoghq.com/logs?query=service%3Aruntime-core-api%20status%3Aerror&from_ts=1779555600000&to_ts=1779559500000&live=false
  • DD metric (p95 spike): https://app.datadoghq.com/metric/explorer?live=false&page=0&exp_metric=trace.aspnet_core.request&exp_scope=env%3Aprod%2Cservice%3Aruntime-core-api%2Cresource_name%3Apost_%2Fapi%2Fv1%2Fruntime%2Fload%2F_screenid%2A&exp_agg=p95&start=1779555900&end=1779559800
  • Kibana: URL unavailable (set KIBANA_BASE_URL in .env)
